name: Authenticated Encryption Assessment
description: Assessment of authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD) constructions including AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-CCM, and AES-SIV. Covers correctness of authentication tag verification, associated data handling, nonce management for AEAD schemes, identification of insecure composition patterns such as MAC-then-encrypt, and evaluation of encrypt-then-MAC implementations.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to authenticated encryption concepts

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the need for authenticated encryption and the risks of encryption without authentication
evidence: Can explain why encryption alone does not provide integrity
Understands the difference between encrypt-then-MAC, MAC-then-encrypt, and AEAD constructions
Can name common AEAD schemes (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies AEAD usage and basic misconfigurations under supervision
evidence: Detects absence of authentication in symmetric encryption deployments
Identifies AES-GCM nonce reuse risks under guidance
Reviews code for correct authentication tag verification practices
Documents AEAD-related findings following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses AEAD implementations for correctness and security
evidence: Evaluates AES-GCM deployments for nonce uniqueness, tag length, and AAD handling
Identifies missing or incorrectly verified authentication tags in application code
Assesses whether encrypt-then-MAC compositions are correctly implemented
Produces actionable findings with references to NIST SP 800-38D/38C or relevant RFCs (RFC 5116, RFC 8439, RFC 8452)

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex AEAD deployments; identifies subtle composition flaws
evidence: Demonstrates GCM nonce-reuse key recovery attacks in lab environments
Evaluates custom AEAD compositions in proprietary protocols
Assesses nonce-misuse-resistant schemes (AES-SIV, AES-GCM-SIV) and their trade-offs
Mentors junior staff on AEAD assessment methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines AEAD assessment methodology; publishes research on authenticated encryption
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's AEAD assessment methodology
Published research on AEAD implementation vulnerabilities or novel attacks
Provides expert guidance on AEAD scheme selection for protocol design
Trains teams on authenticated encryption internals and failure modes

assessment_methods.description: Assess an application using AES-GCM: verify nonce management, tag verification, and AAD handling; demonstrate impact of any identified weaknesses
Given a protocol using MAC-then-encrypt, identify the composition weakness and propose a migration path to a proper AEAD construction
